financials_interim.notes: Arpico Insurance PLC (AINS) -- single-entity filing (Company only; no subsidiaries, no Group/Company split anywhere in the document, sole heading throughout is 'Arpico Insurance PLC'); stored as one GROUP-basis row per this project's convention for single-entity filings (ABL/JINS precedent). This is AINS's FIRST financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB. AINS is a COMPOSITE insurer writing both general and life business under one income statement (Note 7/9/12 reference a distinct 'life insurance fund' and 'change in contract liabilities - life fund', and Note 9 confirms 'No surplus or deficit transfer has been made from the life insurance fund to the Income Statement') but the filing does NOT provide a segmental (life vs general) split of the income statement or balance sheet -- only a combined P&L, so no segment-level figures are stored. Uses the SIX-MONTH CUMULATIVE 'For the period ended 30 June' statements (p.2, balance sheet p.6, cash flow p.8), not the separately-disclosed 'For three months ended 30 June' Q2-only statements on p.4-5. FIELD MAPPING: revenue = the filing's own 'Total net revenue' subtotal (Rs.914,721,889 vs Rs.1,096,222,061 LY, p.2) = Net written premium (Rs.663,139,950, itself GWP Rs.703,753,197 less Premium ceded to reinsurers Rs.40,613,247) + Total Other revenue (Rs.251,581,939 = Fees & commission income Rs.7,297,333 + Investment income Rs.236,336,677 + Fair value gains Rs.6,824,415 + Other operating revenue Rs.1,123,514) -- i.e. materially the task's prescribed 'Net Earned Premium + Investment/Other Income' concept, using the insurer's own disclosed subtotal. operating_profit left BLANK: the P&L has no intermediate subtotal at all -- it proceeds directly from Total net revenue less Total benefits/claims/expenses to Profit before Taxation, with no operating-profit line. finance_costs left BLANK: no separate finance-cost line appears on the face of the income statement; a lease finance cost of Rs.13,178,998 is disclosed only within Note 10's lease-liability roll-forward and is embedded inside 'Other operating, administrative and selling expenses' on the P&L face, not separately broken out -- consistent with the AAIC/JINS precedent of leaving finance_costs blank when not cleanly disclosed as its own P&L line. finance_income left BLANK: Investment income (Rs.236,336,677, Note 6 -- Interest income on held-to-maturity, loans & receivables and AFS assets) is presented as part of insurance revenue (within Total Other revenue), not as a distinct non-insurance finance-income line, matching the AAIC/JINS precedent. gross_profit/cost_of_sales left blank (no COGS concept for an insurer). depreciation_amortization = Rs.61,876,892 (P&L face line, vs Rs.68,965,489 LY). minority_interest left blank (single-entity Company filing, no NCI). Balance sheet is liquidity-ordered (no current/non-current split), so current_assets/current_liabilities left blank, matching AAIC/JINS precedent. inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per the task's insurer guidance: the closest asset-side analogues are Premium receivable (Rs.66,702,928) and Reinsurance receivables (Rs.14,734,766), and on the liability side Reinsurance payables (Rs.6,362,738) -- all insurance-specific items, not generic trade receivables/payables, so excluded from those fields rather than force-mapped. cash_and_equivalents = Rs.93,027,531 (balance sheet 'Cash and cash equivalents', ties exactly to the cash-flow statement's closing balance). short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings left BLANK: the only debt-like balance-sheet item is 'Lease liabilities' (Rs.177,379,557 vs Rs.234,433,002 FY2025), which this project treats as an operating-lease obligation rather than a borrowings/debt draw (no bank loan, debenture, or other conventional borrowings line exists on this balance sheet) -- left out of both borrowings fields rather than force-mapped, consistent with how Insurance contract liabilities (Rs.3,109,625,329) are correctly excluded from borrowings too. capex = Rs.1,506,998, 'Acquisition of property, plant and equipment' (cash flow statement, p.8); 'Net Acquisition of ROU Asset' (Rs.56,170,883) was kept separate and not folded into capex, consistent with a PPE-only capex definition. cash_from_operations = Rs.(380,001,580) -- 'Net cash generated from operating activities' is actually a net OUTFLOW this period (LY H1 2025 was also a net outflow of Rs.(173,208,585)), driven by a working-capital swing in 'Other operating cash flows' of Rs.(497,698,623). cash_from_investing = Rs.384,602,745: NOTE -- the filing's own line is labelled 'Net Cash Used in Investing Activities' but is printed as a POSITIVE number and is arithmetically a net cash INFLOW (Proceeds from sale/maturity of investments Rs.578,215,010 + Interest/dividend received Rs.236,336,677 exceeded Acquisition of financial investments Rs.372,271,061 + PPE additions Rs.1,506,998 + ROU asset additions Rs.56,170,883); this is a labelling error in the source filing (says 'Used' but the sign and the underlying arithmetic show a net inflow) -- the figure is stored as disclosed (positive = net inflow) and this discrepancy is flagged here rather than silently 'corrected'. cash_from_financing = 0 (no financing cash flows this period or LY). shares_in_issue = 66,230,407 (Note 16/20, Twenty Largest Shareholders total), cross-checked against EPS: PAT Rs.22,889,584 / 66,230,407 = Rs.0.3456, rounds to the disclosed Basic EPS of Rs.0.35 exactly; also ties to disclosed Net Assets Per Share of Rs.25.83 (Total Equity Rs.1,710,872,122 / 66,230,407 = Rs.25.83). unit_scale = '1' (absolute LKR, NOT thousands -- the income statement and balance sheet are both in whole Rupees; Note 5's '000 column header is a mislabel, its own figures e.g. Premium ceded to reinsurers Rs.40,613,247 match the P&L face absolute-Rupee figure exactly, not a thousands-scaled version). MATERIAL DRIVER OF THE PROFIT DECLINE: PBT fell 51.9% YoY to Rs.32,979,756 from Rs.68,514,214, and the full change bridges exactly: (1) Net written premium fell Rs.151,325,407 (-18.6%, Rs.663,139,950 vs Rs.814,465,357), driven by GWP falling 18.0% to Rs.703,753,197 from Rs.857,853,092 -- the core top-line contraction; (2) Total Other revenue fell Rs.30,174,765 (-10.7%), mainly Investment income declining 11.1% to Rs.236,336,677 from Rs.265,950,414; (3) Net Insurance Benefits and Claims Paid WORSENED (rose) Rs.85,035,117 (+19.3%) to Rs.525,477,945 from Rs.440,442,828 -- a genuine claims-experience deterioration, notable because it rose sharply even as premium income fell, implying a materially higher loss ratio; (4) this was more than offset by a Rs.154,534,021 favourable SWING in 'Change in contract liabilities - life fund' -- from a Rs.8,870,397 CHARGE in H1 2025 to a Rs.145,663,624 RELEASE/benefit in H1 2026 (Note 12: the life insurance fund balance actually DECREASED this period, i.e. a reserve release) -- this swing alone is larger in magnitude than the entire Rs.35,534,458 PBT decline, and is a reserve/actuarial-adjustment item rather than a recurring operating driver, so should be read as flattering the reported result rather than reflecting underlying trading; (5) Underwriting and net acquisition costs fell Rs.60,816,045 (-26.8%) to Rs.165,764,842 from Rs.226,580,887, a genuine favourable cost item tracking the lower premium volume. Net: without the Rs.154.5mn life-fund reserve release, the PBT decline would have been far steeper than the reported 51.9% -- the headline profit fall is better read as a genuine GWP contraction (-18.0%) plus a worsening claims trend (+19.3% claims paid), partly masked by a non-recurring reserve release. Identity checks tie exactly: PBT - tax = PAT (32,979,756 - 10,090,172 = 22,889,584); Total Assets = Total Liabilities + Total Equity (3,526,100,896 + 1,710,872,122 = 5,236,973,018). Page citations: Income Statement p.2, Balance Sheet p.6, Cash Flow p.8, Note 4 (GWP) p.9, Note 6 (Investment income) p.10, Note 12 (Insurance Contract Liabilities / life fund) p.11, Note 16/20 (shares) p.12-13.

interim_updates.note_text: Arpico Insurance PLC (AINS) reported Total net revenue (the filing's own revenue subtotal = Net written premium + Total Other revenue) of Rs.914.72mn for the six months ended 30 June 2026, down 16.6% YoY (H1 2025: Rs.1,096.22mn), and Profit before Taxation fell 51.9% to Rs.32.98mn (H1 2025: Rs.68.51mn); Profit for the Period fell 53.4% to Rs.22.89mn (H1 2025: Rs.49.17mn); Basic EPS fell to Rs.0.35 from Rs.0.74. The Rs.35.53mn PBT decline decomposes fully and exactly into five line-item changes (verified by summation): (1) Net written premium fell Rs.151.33mn (-18.6%) to Rs.663.14mn from Rs.814.47mn, driven by Gross Written Premium falling 18.0% to Rs.703.75mn from Rs.857.85mn (Note 4) -- the core top-line contraction and the single largest driver; (2) Total Other revenue fell Rs.30.17mn (-10.7%) to Rs.251.58mn from Rs.281.76mn, mainly Investment income declining 11.1% to Rs.236.34mn from Rs.265.95mn (Note 6); (3) Net Insurance Benefits and Claims Paid WORSENED (rose) Rs.85.04mn (+19.3%) to Rs.525.48mn from Rs.440.44mn -- a genuine claims-experience deterioration, notable because claims rose sharply even as premium income fell, implying a materially higher loss ratio; (4) this was more than offset by a Rs.154.53mn favourable SWING in 'Change in contract liabilities - life fund' -- from a Rs.8.87mn CHARGE in H1 2025 to a Rs.145.66mn RELEASE in H1 2026 (Note 12: the life insurance fund balance actually fell this period, i.e. a reserve release) -- this single swing is LARGER than the entire PBT decline and is a reserve/actuarial-adjustment item, not a recurring operating driver, so it should be read as flattering the reported result rather than reflecting underlying trading momentum; (5) Underwriting and net acquisition costs fell Rs.60.82mn (-26.8%) to Rs.165.76mn from Rs.226.58mn, a genuine favourable cost item tracking the lower premium volume, plus Other operating/admin expenses falling 5.0% to Rs.275.90mn from Rs.290.30mn and D&A falling 10.3% to Rs.61.88mn from Rs.68.97mn. Net effect: without the Rs.154.53mn life-fund reserve release, PBT would have fallen far more steeply than the reported 51.9% -- the headline profit decline is better read as an 18.0% GWP contraction plus a worsening claims trend (claims paid +19.3%), partly masked by a non-recurring reserve release rather than genuine operating improvement. Income Tax Expense fell 47.8% YoY to Rs.10.09mn (H1 2025: Rs.19.34mn), tracking the smaller pretax profit base.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is AINS's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (the filing discloses six-month cumulative 'For the period ended 30 June' figures, and the separately-disclosed 'For three months ended 30 June' Q2-only statements on p.4-5 were not used, consistent with the AAIC/JINS precedent in this DB, so no Q1-2026-only figure is available here to derive a QoQ split without re-reading those pages). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) no segmental (life vs general insurance) split of the income statement or balance sheet is disclosed, despite AINS clearly writing composite business (a distinct 'life insurance fund' with its own contract-liability roll-forward exists per Note 12) -- so the relative contribution/trend of the life book vs the general book cannot be isolated from this filing; (2) no claims-experience commentary explains WHY Net Insurance Benefits and Claims Paid rose 19.3% YoY (Rs.440.44mn to Rs.525.48mn) even as GWP fell 18.0% -- i.e. no line-of-business or claim-type breakdown of the higher loss ratio is given; (3) no narrative explains the Rs.154.53mn favourable swing in the life-fund contract-liability change (Note 12 shows the mechanics -- an actuarial Liability Adequacy Test result -- but not the underlying assumption changes driving it); (4) operating_profit is genuinely NOT DISCLOSED as a distinct filing subtotal -- the P&L proceeds directly from Total net revenue less Total benefits/claims/expenses to Profit before Taxation with no intermediate operating-profit line -- left blank in financial_statements; (5) finance_costs is not separately disclosed on the P&L face (a Rs.13.18mn lease finance cost appears only within Note 10's lease-liability roll-forward, embedded inside opex) -- left blank; (6) the cash flow statement's 'Net Cash Used in Investing Activities' line (Rs.384,602,745) is mislabeled -- it is arithmetically and by sign a net cash INFLOW, not a use of cash -- flagged in financial_statements.notes rather than silently corrected.
interim_updates.takeaway: AINS's 51.9% PBT decline (Rs.68.51mn to Rs.32.98mn) is driven first by an 18.0% GWP contraction (Rs.857.85mn to Rs.703.75mn) and second by a 19.3% rise in claims paid (Rs.440.44mn to Rs.525.48mn) even as premium fell -- a genuine loss-ratio deterioration. The reported decline would have been considerably steeper were it not for a Rs.154.53mn favourable swing in the life-fund reserve movement (Note 12), a non-recurring actuarial item larger than the entire PBT fall -- so the headline 51.9% decline likely UNDERSTATES the deterioration in AINS's core underwriting result this period.

operational_highlights: Total net revenue (Company) Rs.914.72mn, -16.6% YoY (H1 2025: Rs.1,096.22mn); PBT Rs.32.98mn, -51.9% YoY (H1 2025: Rs.68.51mn); PAT Rs.22.89mn, -53.4% YoY (H1 2025: Rs.49.17mn); Basic EPS Rs.0.35 vs Rs.0.74 PY.

Gross Written Premium fell 18.0% YoY to Rs.703.75mn from Rs.857.85mn (Note 4); Net written premium fell 18.6% to Rs.663.14mn from Rs.814.47mn -- the core top-line contraction and the single largest driver of the PBT decline.

Net Insurance Benefits and Claims Paid rose 19.3% YoY to Rs.525.48mn from Rs.440.44mn despite the premium contraction, implying a materially higher loss ratio -- a genuine underwriting quality concern this filing does not explain.

'Change in contract liabilities - life fund' swung Rs.154.53mn favourably, from a Rs.8.87mn charge in H1 2025 to a Rs.145.66mn release in H1 2026 (Note 12, an actuarial Liability Adequacy Test outcome) -- larger than the entire PBT decline and a reserve/non-recurring item that flattered the reported result.
Underwriting and net acquisition costs fell 26.8% YoY to Rs.165.76mn from Rs.226.58mn, tracking the lower premium volume; Investment income fell 11.1% to Rs.236.34mn from Rs.265.95mn.
key_drivers: Gross Written Premium contraction of 18.0% YoY (Rs.703.75mn vs Rs.857.85mn) is the primary top-line driver of the result -- a genuine business-volume decline, not an accounting or timing effect.
Net Insurance Benefits and Claims Paid rose 19.3% YoY (Rs.525.48mn vs Rs.440.44mn) even as premium fell, pointing to a deteriorating loss ratio that is the key underlying negative in this result.

A Rs.154.53mn favourable swing in the life-fund contract-liability change (from a Rs.8.87mn charge to a Rs.145.66mn release) is a reserve/actuarial adjustment that is LARGER than the entire Rs.35.53mn PBT decline -- without it, PBT would have fallen far more steeply than the reported 51.9%, so the headline result overstates underlying operating momentum.
Underwriting and net acquisition costs fell 26.8% YoY (Rs.165.76mn vs Rs.226.58mn), a genuine favourable cost item that partly offset the premium and claims pressures.
